blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: This tree follows the topics and the problem list of NeetCode's roadmap (the NeetCode 150), with a learning page written for this site for each topic. The explanations and Java templates are ours; the problems belong to LeetCode, and each one links to its LeetCode page.

A greedy algorithm makes the choice that looks best **right now** and never reconsiders it. It is fast (usually O(n) or O(n log n)) and short to code, but it is only correct when a *local* best choice is guaranteed to be part of a *global* best answer. Proving that is the real work.

Two arguments justify a greedy choice:

- **Greedy stays ahead.** After every step, the greedy solution is at least as good as any other solution at that step (Jump Game: the farthest reachable index).
- **Exchange argument.** Take any optimal solution and swap its first choice for the greedy choice; the result is no worse (interval scheduling by earliest end).

"minimum number of ...", "maximum ... possible", "can you reach", "schedule", "partition so that", where sorting or a running best would work. If you cannot explain *why* the greedy choice is safe, test it against a counterexample before trusting it.
blocks.title: Signal words

blocks.text:
| Problem | Greedy choice | Why it is safe |
|---|---|---|
| Jump Game | Track the farthest reachable index | If you can reach i, you can reach everything before i too |
| Jump Game II | Jump only when you reach the end of the current range | Each jump extends the range as far as possible |
| Gas Station | If the tank goes negative, restart after that station | No station in between can be a valid start |
| Partition Labels | End a part at the last occurrence of every letter seen | A part must contain all copies of its letters |
| Maximum Subarray (Kadane) | Drop the running sum when it becomes negative | A negative prefix only hurts any later subarray |
| Hand of Straights | Always start a group from the smallest remaining card | The smallest card can only start a group |
Coin change with coins {1, 3, 4} and amount 6: greedy takes 4 + 1 + 1 (three coins); the best is 3 + 3 (two). When the greedy choice cannot be proved, the problem needs DP.
blocks.title: Greedy is tempting and often wrong
GreedyTemplates.java

blocks.text: **What to notice.** Each method is a single pass with a few variables. The hard part of each is the one-sentence **reason** the choice is safe; practise saying it out loud, because that is what an interviewer asks for after the code.

- **Assuming greedy works** without a proof or a counterexample search. Try small inputs by hand.
- **Sorting by the wrong criterion** in scheduling problems (earliest end, not earliest start or shortest).
- **Forgetting the global feasibility check**, such as `total >= 0` in Gas Station.
- **Off-by-one in loops** such as `i < nums.length - 1` in Jump Game II: you do not need to jump from the last index.
- **Greedy versus DP confusion.** If choices interact (taking one item changes what else is possible in complicated ways), use DP.

Either show the greedy solution stays ahead of any other solution after every step, or use an exchange argument: take any optimal solution, replace its first choice with the greedy choice, and show the result is still optimal. If you cannot find such an argument, look for a counterexample or switch to DP.
blocks.title: Interview angle: How do you prove a greedy algorithm correct?
Key points
blocks.text:
- Greedy takes the locally best choice and never revisits it
- It is correct only when the local choice is part of a global optimum: be ready to say why
- "Stays ahead" and exchange arguments are the two standard proofs
- Sorting by the right key is half the problem in scheduling tasks
- Coin change with arbitrary coins is the classic case where greedy fails
- When in doubt, test small cases or fall back to DP

items.question: Why is Kadane's algorithm greedy?
items.answer: It decides at each element whether to extend the current subarray or start fresh, keeping the running sum only while it helps. A negative running sum can only reduce any later subarray, so discarding it is always safe.

items.question: Why does restarting after a failure work in Gas Station?
items.answer: If you cannot reach station j starting from i, you cannot reach it from any station between i and j either, because each of them would arrive at j with no more gas than the run from i did. So the next candidate start is j.

items.question: Give an example where greedy fails.
items.answer: Coin change with coins {1, 3, 4} and amount 6. Greedy picks 4 + 1 + 1 (three coins), but 3 + 3 uses two. A DP over amounts finds the minimum.
